import pandas as pd

# File paths for source data
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_98/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_98/test_1.csv"

# Load Source 0
# Schema: ['right_index', '0']
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path)

# Load Source 1
# Schema: ['0']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path)

# Transformation plan:
# - Target schema: ['0_x': float, '0_y': float]
# - Source 0 has columns ['right_index', '0'], 1000 rows
# - Source 1 has column ['0'], 500 rows
# - Target has 500 rows, so we will align on the 500 rows from Source 1
# - Use Source 1 '0' as '0_y'
# - Use Source 0 '0' column values at indices matching Source 1 index (0 to 499) as '0_x'
#   The 'right_index' in Source 0 seems to be the row index, so we can use df0.loc[df0['right_index'], '0']
#   Since Source 0 has 1000 rows, and Source 1 has 500 rows, we take the first 500 rows from Source 0 matching right_index 0-499
# - Construct target DataFrame with columns '0_x' and '0_y'

# Extract '0_x' from Source 0 for indices 0 to 499
df0_subset = df0[df0['right_index'].between(0, 499)].copy()
df0_subset = df0_subset.sort_values('right_index')  # Ensure sorted by right_index
# Reset index to align with df1
df0_subset.reset_index(drop=True, inplace=True)

# Extract '0_y' from Source 1
df1_subset = df1.copy()
df1_subset.reset_index(drop=True, inplace=True)

# Build target DataFrame
target_df = pd.DataFrame({
    '0_x': df0_subset['0'].astype(float),
    '0_y': df1_subset['0'].astype(float)
})

# Save the target DataFrame to CSV
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_98/target_multisource_cot.csv"
target_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
